subject: ACMEHealth private VPC dataflow privacy follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACMEHealth private VPC dataflow privacy follow-up

Hi Alex / Sarah team,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate you walking us through the use case and privacy constraints. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of the ask: you want a Private (VPC) deployment of Redwood for clinical note summarization and PII extraction.
2) Primary privacy requirements we heard: PII redaction at ingest, maximum retention of 30 days for raw logs, audit logging for model requests, and strict egress controls (no internet egress from the VPC except to your approved endpoints).
3) Desired topology: model inference running in your VPC (customer-managed subnets) with a private control plane and optional on-prem / air-gapped mode for the most sensitive workloads.

Attached is a first-pass dataflow diagram and our Private VPC checklist to help coordinate with your infra/security teams.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme-dataflow-draft.pdf (pdf, 240KB)], [Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 86KB)]

Questions we have for you to unblock qualification:
- Do you have a preferred KMS / HSM for key management, or should we propose our recommended KMS integrations?
- For PII redaction: do you need redaction pre-ingest (client-side) or is server-side acceptable if logs are never persisted beyond 30 days?
- Any whitelist for allowed egress endpoints (e.g., internal telemetry endpoints, artifact registry)?

Next steps: Vivek will schedule a short session with your infra/security folks to walk the checklist and the dataflow. If that works, we can scope a PO for a Private deployment pilot once we align on KMS and egress controls.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: ACMEHealth private VPC dataflow privacy follow-up

Marissa —

Thanks for the notes and the attachments. A couple clarifications from our side:
- For now we'd prefer server-side PII redaction with strict logging controls, provided raw payloads can be set to auto-delete at 30 days and are encrypted at rest with our KMS.
- We need audit logs of model calls (who/when/payload hash) to go to our Splunk instance; can you support forwarding audit logs directly into an on-prem Splunk collector inside the VPC?
- On egress: we cannot have outbound internet egress from the inference hosts. Approved outbound destinations will be our internal artifact registry and your control plane endpoint IPs (we'll provide a list).

I'll get Sarah Patel (security) and our infra lead to join the follow-up. Available windows: Tue 3/2 9-11am PT or Wed 3/3 1-3pm PT.

Alex
From: security@acmehealth.com
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACMEHealth private VPC dataflow privacy follow-up

Hi Marissa / Vivek,

A few technical items our security team needs clarified before we can sign off on a pilot: 
- Key management: we use HashiCorp Vault (self-hosted) with HSM-backed keys. We need to confirm that Redwood can integrate with our Vault via mTLS and that keys never leave our control.
- Logging: audit logs must be write-once to a storage location in our VPC, with Object Lock (WORM) enabled for 90 days. Can Redwood ship logs directly to an S3-compatible endpoint in our VPC?
- Egress controls: we require a strict deny-all outbound policy on inference hosts except for explicit allow rules. Any control plane traffic must be via a customer-managed proxy with mutual TLS.
- Air-gapped option: for PHI workloads we may require an on-prem air-gapped deployment. How mature is Redwood's on-prem deployment and what are the offline activation/auth flows?

Can Vivek or Marissa share the checklist items that map to each of these requirements so we can run them in our risk/controls matrix?

Thanks,
Sarah Patel
Head of Security, ACME Health
security@acmehealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACMEHealth private VPC dataflow privacy follow-up

Alex / Sarah — thanks for laying these out. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

- KMS / Vault: Redwood supports HashiCorp Vault integrations via mTLS and can be configured so that customer keys never leave your control plane. We'll document the exact flow (key wrapping/unwrapping, local CMK usage) in the checklist.
- Audit logs: we can stream audit logs to an S3-compatible endpoint in your VPC; object-lock / WORM can be enabled on your bucket. We'll add guidance around message digests and minimal persisted fields (request id, timestamp, hashed payload).
- Splunk: we can forward audit events to your Splunk collector using a private-forwarder inside the VPC.
- Strict egress: supported — inference hosts can be deployed in private subnets with NAT disabled and explicit allow rules to your artifact registry and control-plane proxy IPs.
- Air-gapped: our on-prem package supports offline activation using signed licenses and an air-gapped installer. We'll include the activation flow and the offline telemetry zero-touch guidance in the doc.

Next steps:
1) I'll schedule a 45-minute technical workshop with your security and infra folks on Tue 3/2 9:30am PT (tentative — Alex please confirm).
2) Marissa / Neha: we've attached an updated checklist that maps each security ask to the configuration or operational control. Please review before the workshop.
3) Post-workshop: Redwood will provide a scoped pilot SOW and a short runbook for the pilot deployment and validations.

Let us know if there are any blockers on the timing.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
